hook_q: Can I get one for free?

slides.title: Yes, many people can.
slides.body: If you have to file or defend a case, the law gives free legal services to certain groups of people.

slides.title: Who qualifies?
list: Members of Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes
People with a disability or mental illness

slides.title: Also covered.
list: Victims of human trafficking or begar (forced labour)
Victims of a mass disaster, ethnic violence, caste atrocity, flood, drought, earthquake or industrial disaster
People whose yearly income is below the limit set by their State

slides.title: What "free" covers.
slides.body: A lawyer paid by the State, your court fee, and other case expenses. The Legal Services Authority first checks that you have a genuine case.

slides.title: How to ask for it.
list: Call 15100, NALSA's toll-free legal aid helpline
Apply online on NALSA's legal aid portal
Visit the District Legal Services Authority at your district court

caption:
Can't afford a lawyer? You may be entitled to one for free. 👇

Under Section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, these people get free legal services:
• Every woman and child
• SC/ST members
• People with a disability or mental illness
• Industrial workers
• Anyone in custody
• Victims of trafficking, disasters, ethnic violence or caste atrocities
• People with income below their State's limit

It covers a lawyer, court fees and case expenses.
📞 Call NALSA's free helpline: 15100

Sources: Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 (Sec 12); nalsa.gov.in
